title: SIR vs SSR: Voter rolls in 13 states and UTs add 74.66 lakh names, register 1.65% rise
shows: Deccan Herald sets the draft rolls of the special summary revision in 13 states and union territories against the final rolls of the intensive revision and reports about 74.66 lakh names added, a rise of 1.65% from 45.22 crore to 45.96 crore, in states and union territories that held 49.61 crore electors before the intensive revision. It gives the largest rise in numbers to Uttar Pradesh, 18.84 lakh or 1.4%, from 13.39 crore to 13.58 crore, and puts Bihar next, with its roll rising from 7.42 crore to 7.55 crore. It gives Rajasthan 11.47 lakh or 2.23%, Tamil Nadu 10.39 lakh or 1.83%, Kerala 4.06 lakh or 1.51%, Chhattisgarh 2.85 lakh or 1.53%, Assam 2.18 lakh or 0.88%, Uttarakhand 1.19 lakh or 1.66%, Manipur 33,737 or 1.72%, Puducherry 12,786 or 1.35% and Lakshadweep 94 or 0.16%. It puts the largest rise in proportion in Goa, 3.01%, from 10.57 lakh to 10.89 lakh. It reports that drafts had been published in 15 states, with no data for Punjab and Gujarat, and that the summary revision was announced in Karnataka and Meghalaya on 16 November. It reports that the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised concerns over the delay in holding the summary revision in states where the intensive revision had finished. It reports that parties will now be given the draft and final rolls free of cost as readable PDFs without photographs of the electors, along with a physical copy, after the Commission had refused machine-readable rolls.
quote: These states and UTs had 49.61 crore voters before the SIR and had declined to 45.22 crore during the contentious exercise.
It has now grown to 45.96 crore, registering a 1.65% rise from the final rolls published after the SIR.
note: First reading, 18 November 2026. Read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 18 November 2026, which marks it isAccessibleForFree true. Byline Shemin Joy, New Delhi, datePublished 2026-11-17T21:11:34+05:30. Checked against data/india/raw/ssr_draft.csv and final.csv. Uttar Pradesh agrees (13,58,68,905 against 13,39,84,792, 18,84,113 more, 1.41%). Rajasthan agrees (11,47,487, 2.23%), Tamil Nadu agrees (10,39,238, 1.83%), Kerala agrees (4,06,610, 1.51%), Chhattisgarh agrees within rounding (2,85,854, 1.53%), Uttarakhand agrees (1,19,086, 1.66%), and Manipur (33,737, 1.72%), Puducherry (12,786, 1.35%) and Lakshadweep (94, 0.16%) agree exactly. Assam's 2.18 lakh and 0.88% agree with the net rise of 2,18,771 in the file, from 4,12,344 added and 1,93,573 deleted since the final roll of its special revision. Four figures disagree with the file and are not carried. Goa's rise is printed as 31,185, where the file has 10,89,381 against 10,57,566, a rise of 31,815, which The New Indian Express also gives, and the paper's own 10.57 lakh, 10.89 lakh and 3.01% agree with 31,815. Madhya Pradesh is printed as 8.90 lakh or 1.65%, where the file has 8,18,563 or 1.52% from PTI and Dainik Bhaskar. Bihar is printed as 13.89 lakh or 1.87%, where the file has 13,97,008 or 1.88% against the final roll of 30 September 2025. The site's figures for the 13 add to 73,95,162 more, from 45,22,07,173 to 45,96,02,335, a rise of 1.64%. The paper's 45.22 crore and 45.96 crore agree with those, and its 74.66 lakh and 1.65% are about 71,000 higher, which is close to the difference in Madhya Pradesh. The 49.61 crore before the intensive revision cannot be checked, because the site holds no roll for Assam before its special revision. The 12 other states and union territories held 47,09,76,736 before the intensive revision in states.csv. The report's account of the disagreement among the Election Commissioners is the paper's and is summarised only as it states it. The Hindu's report of the same day by Sreeparna Chakrabarty is for subscribers and was not read.
